claims.text: FSD of AlCrFeNiSi powder produces components with substantially lower residual thermal stress than LPBF.
FSD of AlCrFeNiSi powder produces finer equiaxed microstructures than LPBF.
FSD of AlCrFeNiSi powder produces improved mechanical properties relative to LPBF.
Vacuum-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder in the 15–45 μm range has homogeneous composition.
An applicable FSD window is 1000–2000 rpm, 50–150 mm/min traverse speed, 0.3–1.0 mm layer thickness, and an inert atmosphere.
The proposed process is valid for feature sizes up to 20 mm, component thicknesses up to 5 mm, and ambient-temperature mechanical testing.
FSD produces ultrafine equiaxed grains of approximately 1 μm in AlCrFeNiSi.
The ultrafine equiaxed grains are formed by dynamic recrystallization.
FSD eliminates columnar solidification structures in the deposited AlCrFeNiSi.
Severe plastic deformation during FSD drives dynamic recrystallization.
FSD proceeds in the solid state and therefore avoids melting and rapid solidification.
Avoiding melting and rapid solidification reduces thermal gradients relative to LPBF.
Reduced thermal gradients cause lower locked-in residual stress.
FSD components will have residual stress below 30 MPa, compared with approximately 200 MPa for the stated LPBF baseline.
FSD components will have an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 480 MPa, compared with approximately 400 MPa for the stated LPBF baseline.
FSD components will have approximately 6.5% elongation to failure, compared with approximately 5% for the stated LPBF baseline.
LPBF at 200 W, 1200 mm/s, a 30 μm layer thickness, and no preheat produces approximately 200 MPa residual stress in this material.
LPBF at the stated baseline settings produces approximately 400 MPa UTS and 5% elongation in this material.
FSD is established for aluminum alloys.
Direct FSD data for AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloy are limited.
